column1: # What a person has excepted, for a while, from blocking a task.
# A row here clears ONE admitted obligation of class TASK_BLOCKING at the task
# moment — the gate and the Stop hook — and nothing else: never a
# RELEASE_BLOCKING or AUTHORITY_BLOCKING row, never the merge boundary, never
# an escape channel. A release-blocking obligation somebody wants past is a
# policy decision, not an exception (amendments §3).
# obligation
#   obligation  the ledger name in obligations.tsv this grant is for.
#   row_hash    `git hash-object --stdin` of that row's exact line, newline
#               included — `felix obligations` prints it beside each row so it
#               can be copied. Twelve or more hex characters of it. The grant
#               is void the moment the row changes in any column, reason
#               included: an obligation cannot be rewritten under a live grant.
#   expires     an absolute UTC stamp, YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ. Refused once
#               passed; refused in any other shape.
#   granted_by  the person, as text. The commit that merged the row is the
#               attestation.
#   reason      why, for whoever reads this ledger later.
# WHERE IT IS READ FROM. Never this working tree. The engine reads this file
# from refs/remotes/origin/main — the remote-tracking main, never a local
# branch, which a session could move — of the repository that holds it, so a
# row a session writes here clears nothing until it is merged and fetched, and
# merging it is an escape (`exception`) that felix merge hands to a person.
# That is what makes the grant a person's act and not a command a session
# can invoke. `felix obligations` still lists rows found only in the working
# tree, marked as not yet a grant, so what was written can be seen before it
# is merged.
# Missing, malformed, expired, moved, or naming a row that no longer matches:
# all read as no clearance, identically. Nothing here can waive an obligation;
# it can only defer one, until a date, with a name beside it.
# Seeded empty by felix new. A project that never writes a row here is a
# project that never needed one, which is the common case.
